current45Profile.applicability: The same Runner implementation governs ordinary selected xpcshell stages. The ownership gap predates and does not require the future Node profile. Fatal or natural primary exit followed by cleanup is a relevant source path.
current45Profile.currentRuntimeEvidence: No actual reuse or foreign signal was observed in this review. Existing stage outcomes remain their recorded outcomes; this review does not infer the active run failed or supply its cause.
current45Profile.operationalAction: No polling, cancellation, extra job, CI/ref mutation or source change was performed. The active run is not stopped based on this modeled issue.
current45Profile.qualificationLimit: Existing leaderReap and verified-gone receipts do not, by themselves, prove that every earlier signal targeted the original group epoch under this counterexample.

finding.conclusion: Existing guards do not prevent a successful numeric existence probe from authorizing signals to a later foreign group using the reaped primary PID/PGID.
confirmedAtSourceLevel: Direct stop on an already-reaped primary sends SIGINT to the modeled foreign epoch.
owned_group_alive itself can reap then accept a reused numeric group.
The last old member can disappear after the successful existence probe, with a replacement foreign group receiving the following SIGINT.
The PermissionError/newly-reaped recheck also accepts a different epoch when the later numeric probe succeeds.
Actual run paths with modeled exit zero or nonzero can send the foreign signal, then report exact leader reaping and verified-gone cleanup.
Reuse introduced only in the final finally block can send the foreign signal while Runner.run returns normally with exitCode zero, reason null, cleanupFailure null, verified-gone and failure null.
finding.missingInvariant: The signal path has no unreaped exact-child reservation or other kernel-held group-epoch authority after poll/wait; killpg(pgid,0) proves existence/access at that moment, not ownership or epoch continuity.
finding.modelRestriction: No model replaces a continuously populated old group. Numeric reuse is introduced only after all old members and the old session have gone and the primary was reaped.

finding.priorityScope: Source-level signal-ownership and successful-cleanup qualification; blocks admitting a new fatal-cleanup profile on unchanged Runner. It does not attribute an incident to the current CI.
finding.trigger: The original leader was reaped; all old process-group/session members disappear; that numeric PID becomes available and a foreign process starts a new same-number group before a cleanup probe or signal.

futureExternalRealService.admission: No new external-service ownership/cleanup PASS profile until the shared primary cleanup authority is fixed/reviewed and real Mac failure probes pass. The route can remain narrower than a broker, but not by assuming this unverified invariant.
futureExternalRealService.correctedLimit: The previous comparison must not be read as certification of fatal-exit cleanup safety inherited from unchanged Runner. That primary cleanup authority has now been independently disproved under the modeled reuse ordering.
futureExternalRealService.fatalHarnessOwnerLoss: If the exact-child QA owner lives in the harness and the harness fatally exits, its Node child may be reparented; that owner cannot supply a later matched wait. Outer numeric PGID cleanup alone does not repair that missing authority.
futureExternalRealService.retainedClaim: A same-primary-PGID real service naturally enters the existing group resource sample while its membership is valid.

kernelReference.qualification: Tagged primary source is a semantic reference, not evidence of selected runner runtime state or measured reuse frequency.

sources.basis: Reap removes the child from its process group and process hash, then releases the group reference.
Last-member removal marks the group empty; final release destroys it, removes its hash entry and releases the session.
A process can form its own new-session group only when it is not already that group leader and no same-ID group is found.

minimumRemediationChoices.limitation: This prevents using stale numeric authority but cannot drain live orphan descendants after fatal leader exit; it is insufficient alone for a successful future service cleanup proof.
minimumRemediationChoices.scope: Stop issuing nonzero group signals once the exact direct-child anchor has been reaped or its ownership is unknown. Independent exact-child wait/evidence may continue. Missing safe group retirement must remain cleanup-unconfirmed and fail qualification.

minimumRemediationChoices.choice: Retain exact primary anchor through drainage
minimumRemediationChoices.limitation: Requires deliberate changes to the primary run poll/wait/cleanup path or explicit launch semantics. Preserve clocks/resource limits and first-failure evidence. No such implementation is supplied by this review.
minimumRemediationChoices.scope: Use a reviewed non-reaping observation/terminal-barrier protocol or an owned session-leader guardian so a genuine unreaped direct child reserves the group epoch until all nonleaders are drained. Serialize signals with the sole reaper, then matched wait and fresh retirement.

minimumRemediationChoices.choice: Do not substitute cached identity checks
minimumRemediationChoices.limitation: Any alternative kernel-bound handle/anchor contract must be separately proven on the actual selected platform.
minimumRemediationChoices.scope: A generation check immediately before a later numeric signal is useful evidence but does not itself close the post-reap query-to-signal race. PID/name/UID scans, groups membership or an earlier complete census are insufficient replacement authority.

requiredMacProofAfterPatch: Exact owned leader lives, exits to unreaped zombie, remains the bound group anchor through descendant drainage, and is waited exactly once only after anchor-only state.
Harness fatal exit while a real service/pipe-holding child survives: no lost owner, no false live/zero status, no numeric signal after anchor loss and independent cleanup result.
Natural zero exit and nonzero/signal exit, plus late finally, all preserve first cause and no cleanup PASS if signal authority becomes unavailable.

Deterministic foreign-epoch, last-member-departure, reaper/ECHILD, denied-query and duplicate-stop fault injections reject before any OS signal to a foreign target; real reuse stress is not needed to send foreign signals.
Existing normal stages, resource/helper deadlines and original job clock stay unchanged; monitor failure/cleanup evidence remains separate.
scope: Read-only independent review of existing primary process-group cleanup after the exact leader has been reaped. This is not evidence that the active CI run reused a PID or signaled a foreign group.

sourceAnchorCorrection.reason: The earlier line numbers did not identify the stated operations in the named fixed tag. Independent raw reads confirmed the exact file bytes and corrected locations.

whyExistingGuardsDoNotRefute.assessment: Stores/removes only numeric PGIDs. stop does not consult it, and membership would not distinguish epochs even if it did.
Explicitly diagnostic-only and never consulted to authorize primary group signals. A stale list is not a kernel-held reservation.
Calls killpg with signal zero; success contains no PID birth, SID generation or owned epoch information.
Limits one denied-path retry to a newly reaped leader, but the retry is still the same numeric probe. The success path does not enter this guard at all.
poll and wait may already have reaped the exact primary before every later cleanup probe. finally can signal a newly existing group without recording a new failure if that cleanup returns normally.
Provides separately bound native-process evidence; it is not a gate on the primary stop killpg call.
Existence is not ownership. After anchor loss, a separate fresh query cannot make query-then-killpg atomic against last-member departure and number reuse.
